findings.evidence: <body id="body">; 2 focusable element(s) precede the first heading
findings.fix: Add a <main> element wrapping the primary content, or a skip link as the first focusable element linking to it.
findings.violation: The page provides neither a main landmark (a <main> element or role="main") nor a leading same-page skip link.

findings.fix: Give the page a specific <title> describing its topic or purpose.
findings.violation: The page has no usable title: the title element is missing or empty.

findings.evidence: The only navigation mechanism on the page is the primary nav (Plan a trip, Accessibility); no search form, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail appears anywhere in the document.
findings.fix: Add a second, independent way to find this page, such as a site search, a sitemap link, or a breadcrumb trail reflecting the page's place in the site.
findings.violation: The page relies solely on the primary navigation menu to be located within the site, with no second independent mechanism such as a search, sitemap, or breadcrumb trail, and the page is not one step of a linear process that would exempt it.

findings.fix: Set lang to a well-formed BCP 47 tag identifying the page's default language, for example lang="en".
findings.violation: The <html> element's lang attribute 'translanguage' is not a well-formed BCP 47 language tag.

findings.fix: Add an alt attribute (or aria-label) describing the image, or mark it decorative with alt="".
findings.violation: No text alternative is present and the element is not marked decorative.

findings.fix: Change this heading to <h3>, or add the missing intervening heading level.
findings.violation: Heading level skips from <h2> to <h4> with no intervening level.

findings.fix: Rewrite the link text to describe its destination or purpose, or add an aria-label.
findings.violation: The link's accessible name is a generic phrase that gives no clue to its destination out of context.

findings.evidence:
Riders can check real time arrivals at any station kiosk. Station staff can also help with the same request in person.

sits under the 'Fare adjustments' heading alongside the fare-adjustment paragraph.
findings.fix: Move the real-time-arrivals paragraph to a section whose heading covers it, or split this section under two headings that each match their own content.
findings.violation: The second paragraph in this section describes checking real-time arrivals, a different topic than the heading promises, so a reader scanning headings for arrival information would not look here and one that scans for fare information gets an unrelated paragraph mixed in.

findings.evidence: Section content under this heading: "Passengers can report a service issue by calling rider services. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day." plus a zone status table (#s2-table1); none of it concerns accessibility improvements.
findings.fix: Retitle the heading to match the section's actual content, such as 'Service issues and zone status', or move this content under a heading that already covers it.
findings.violation: The heading's wording describes a topic (accessibility improvements) that the section's actual content never addresses, so a reader scanning headings to find accessibility information is misdirected here and finds service-issue and zone-status content instead.
